item.title: Nominations open for 2027 Fenland Citizen Business Awards
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Nominations open for 2027 Fenland Citizen Business Awards
Nominations are now being accepted for the 2027 Fenland Citizen Business Awards. Accountancy firm Whitings LLP, which has offices in March, Wisbech, and Ely, has returned as the headline sponsor for the event. The awards recognise local success across eight categories, including Business of the Year, Best New Start-Up, and Employer of the Year.
Businesses, individuals, and charities are encouraged to enter before the deadline at 5pm on Wednesday, January 6. The winners will be announced during a black-tie ceremony held at the Wisbech St Mary Sports and Community Centre on Friday, March 19, 2027. Further details regarding entry criteria and categories are available on the Fenland Business Awards website.

item.title: Norfolk County Council confirms David Walliams books to remain in libraries
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Norfolk County Council confirms David Walliams books to remain in libraries
Norfolk County Council has announced that books by author David Walliams will stay on library shelves across the county. Despite recent allegations of misconduct against the comedian, the council confirmed that titles including Gangsta Granny and Mr Stink remain available for loan.
Councillor Pat Gould stated that the authority follows established ethical principles regarding its collections. The council maintains that books are kept unless there is a legal reason for their removal. Officials added that all library stock is subject to regular reviews to ensure collections meet the needs of local residents.

item.title: Norfolk zoo founder and conservationist Ken Sims dies aged 85
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Norfolk zoo founder and conservationist Ken Sims dies aged 85
Tributes have been paid to Ken Sims, the founder of Thrigby Hall Wildlife Gardens, who has died at the age of 85. Born and raised in King’s Lynn, Mr Sims passed away on October 25. He established the popular Norfolk attraction in 1979 and was widely recognised for his global contributions to animal conservation.
Throughout his career, Mr Sims served as a zoo inspector and held senior roles with the Zoological Society of London. Colleagues have praised his vision and determination, noting his significant work in protecting threatened species. His family, who remain local to the King’s Lynn area, described him as a highly respected figure in the international animal community.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/highly-respected-norfolk-zoo-founder-dies-aged-85-9491344/

item.title: Concerns raised over potential service cuts in West Norfolk
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Concerns raised over potential service cuts in West Norfolk
Liberal Democrat councillor Rob Colwell is calling for greater transparency regarding proposed service cuts across West Norfolk. While the Queen Elizabeth Hospital’s 24-hour A&E remains protected, maternity and children’s inpatient services are still under review.
Meanwhile, Norfolk County Council is considering budget reductions that could impact road maintenance, including a five per cent cut to the priority gritting network. Other proposals include increased costs for post-16 transport and reduced household waste disposal services. Councillor Colwell is urging residents to participate in ongoing public consultations before the December deadlines. The main budget consultation closes on December 7, with the post-16 transport consultation ending on December 15. Residents are encouraged to share how these potential changes would affect their daily lives.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/west-norfolk-deserves-answers-before-services-are-cut-9490844/

item.title: New documentary to capture the history of West Norfolk
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
New documentary to capture the history of West Norfolk
A new 60-minute documentary, currently in development, aims to preserve the history and achievements of West Norfolk for future generations. Titled ‘Under the West Norfolk Skies’, the film is a partnership between West Norfolk Council and the Lynn-based production company RFA Media.
The project will explore ten key themes, including local industry, royal connections, and the area’s relationship with the River Great Ouse. It will examine the borough’s development since 1974 while tracing its deeper historical roots. The production team is currently gathering archive material and conducting interviews, with plans to make sections of the film available across digital platforms to ensure the borough's story remains accessible to a wide audience.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Plans submitted to convert former Wisbech funeral home into nine dwellings
A planning application has been submitted to Fenland District Council to transform a vacant former funeral home on Alexandra Road in Wisbech. The proposal, put forward by Andrew Bennett on behalf of Fitzroy Highgate Ltd, seeks to create six houses and three flats at the site.
The project involves demolishing part of the existing structure facing Love Lane to make way for a new two-storey building. The plans also include a small second-floor extension on the Alexandra Road side. If approved, the development will retain an outdoor courtyard for resident use, with potential space for cycle storage. The site has remained empty for more than three years.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Caring Together Charity opens first shop in King’s Lynn
A new charity shop has opened its doors in King’s Lynn town centre today. Located on the High Street at the site of the former Cancer Research store, the shop is the first fundraising outlet for Caring Together. The charity provides advice and support to unpaid carers across Norfolk, Cambridgeshire, and Peterborough.
Manager Belinda Jones says the shop is now accepting donations of clothing, homeware, and toys between 9am and 4pm, Monday to Saturday. The team is also looking for new volunteers to help with the venture. Proceeds from the shop will fund essential services for those caring for family members or friends with long-term illnesses or disabilities. Further details are available on the charity’s website.

New art exhibition opens at Wisbech Gallery
A new exhibition featuring three local emerging artists has opened at the Wisbech Gallery. Titled Flare, the showcase displays work by Ruby Bellamy, Kayleigh Brooks, and Lily Rolfe, covering themes ranging from local landscapes to human emotions. The exhibition was opened by award-winning artist EVES and will remain on display until Saturday, November 28, 2026.
In addition to the exhibition, the gallery is hosting free weekly Sketch and Social sessions every Saturday throughout November from 11am to 3pm. The gallery is open to the public Wednesday through Saturday, between 10am and 4pm. Admission to both the exhibition and the social sessions is free of charge.

item.description:

Thousands of crocus bulbs planted in King’s Lynn to support polio campaign
Volunteers from the Rotary Club of Lynn have planted 16,000 purple crocus bulbs at the Edward Benefer Way roundabout. The display, completed on Sunday, November 8, aims to raise awareness for the global effort to eradicate polio. The purple flowers represent the dye used to mark children who have received immunisations.
The project follows a similar planting event last year and recent efforts to highlight the Polio Plus campaign, including lighting up the Corn Exchange in purple. The bulbs were sponsored by Health and Community Construction, with additional support provided by the St James Health Centre. Rotary International has been working towards the global elimination of the disease since 1985.

King’s Lynn care home regains ‘good’ rating
Amberley Hall Care Home in King’s Lynn has been rated ‘good’ by the Care Quality Commission following a recent inspection. The facility, located on Baldock Drive, has successfully exited special measures three years after previously being rated ‘inadequate’.
Inspectors assessed the home across five key areas, including safety and leadership, finding that residents receive personalised care and are encouraged to maintain their independence. The report also highlighted improvements in care planning and the home’s partnership with the Integrated Care Board to support hospital discharges. Manager Blessy Masilamani credited the turnaround to the dedication and resilience of the staff team over the past year.
